/-!
# Conjecture 8.9

by R. I. Grigorchuk

(C. Chou). We say that a group $G$ has *property $P$* if for every finite subset $F$ of $G$,
there is a finite subset $S \supseteq F$ and a subset $X \subseteq G$ such that
$x_1 S \cap x_2 S$ is empty for any $x_1, x_2 \in X$, $x_1 \ne x_2$, and
$G = \bigcup_{x \in X} S x$. Does every group have property $P$?

Note the asymmetry in the definition: the *left* translates $x S$, $x \in X$, are required to
be pairwise disjoint, while the *right* translates $S x$, $x \in X$, are required to cover $G$.
The set $X$ is not required to be finite.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.code:
def HasPropertyP (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ F : Finset G, ∃ S : Finset G, F ⊆ S ∧ ∃ X : Set G,
    X.PairwiseDisjoint (fun x => x • (S : Set G)) ∧
    ⋃ x ∈ X, op x • (S : Set G) = Set.univ
blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ has *property $P$* (in the sense of C. Chou) if for every finite subset $F$ of $G$
there are a finite subset $S \supseteq F$ of $G$ and a subset $X \subseteq G$ such that the left
translates $x S$, $x \in X$, are pairwise disjoint, i.e. $x_1 S \cap x_2 S = \emptyset$ for all
$x_1, x_2 \in X$ with $x_1 \ne x_2$, and the right translates $S x$, $x \in X$, cover $G$, i.e.
$G = \bigcup_{x \in X} S x$.

Here the left translate $x S$ is `x • (S : Set G)` and the right translate $S x$ is
`op x • (S : Set G)`, following the Mathlib convention for right cosets.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib has left/right cosets of subgroups (`x • ↑H`, `MulOpposite.op x • ↑H`) and `Set.PairwiseDisjoint`, which are used as building blocks, but nothing packaging the 'for every finite F there is a finite S ⊇ F and X with disjoint xS and covering Sx' property. The repo's tiling files (Paper/WeakTiling.lean, Arxiv/2209.04540) concern Euclidean/measure-theoretic weak tilings, not group-theoretic ones.
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.9».HasPropertyP
justification.why_needed: The notebook defines 'property P' ad hoc inside the problem statement; no notion of a group admitting such asymmetric (left-disjoint / right-covering) finite 'tilings' exists in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib. The definition is problem-specific, so it is kept in the problem file (per STATEMENTS.md) together with a `@[category test]` lemma that every finite group has property P (S = G, X = {1}).

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem hasPropertyP_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : HasPropertyP G := by
  intro F
  cases nonempty_fintype G
  refine ⟨Finset.univ, Finset.subset_univ F, {1}, Set.pairwiseDisjoint_singleton _ _, ?_⟩
  simp

claims.decomposer_note: Single unlettered yes/no question (answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ groups G, G has property P) where property P is the auxiliary definition given verbatim in the statement; note the deliberate left/right asymmetry that must be preserved — disjointness is of the LEFT translates x₁S ∩ x₂S = ∅ for distinct x₁, x₂ ∈ X, while the covering is by RIGHT translates G = ⋃_{x∈X} Sx, with S finite and S ⊇ F for an arbitrary finite F ⊆ G, and X an arbitrary (not necessarily finite) subset of G.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates are mathematically faithful and compile cleanly: each preserves the left/right asymmetry (LEFT translates xS pairwise disjoint over distinct x in X, RIGHT translates Sx cover G), keeps S finite with F ⊆ S for an arbitrary finite F, leaves X an arbitrary Set G, and quantifies `∀ (G : Type) [Group G]` per the Kourovka convention. I verified in scratch files that `x • S = {x} * S = (x * ·) '' S`, `op x • S = S * {x} = (· * x) '' S`, and that `Set.PairwiseDisjoint` unfolds to the required distinct-pair disjointness; I also proved that c04's `HasPropertyP` is equivalent to a literal elementwise transcription of Chou's definition. c04 was chosen because the decomposition table treats property P as an auxiliary definition and CONTRIBUTING.md asks for bespoke definitions to carry API tests: c04 gives a clean `HasPropertyP` using the Mathlib coset idiom (`x • S` / `op x • S`) with `Finset`, a proved `@[category test]` lemma that finite groups have property P, and complete docstrings on both the definition and the main theorem (c03's main docstring is terse; c02 mixes `•` and `*` notations; c01/c06/c07/c08 inline the property without a definition or test). Shipped unchanged.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The single-slot decomposition with the auxiliary definition, the left/right asymmetry note, and the arbitrary (not necessarily finite) X all match the source text.

/-!
# Conjecture 8.9

by R. I. Grigorchuk

(C. Chou). We say that a group $G$ has *property $P$* if for every finite subset $F$ of $G$,
there is a finite subset $S \supseteq F$ and a subset $X \subseteq G$ such that
$x_1 S \cap x_2 S$ is empty for any $x_1, x_2 \in X$, $x_1 \ne x_2$, and
$G = \bigcup_{x \in X} S x$. Does every group have property $P$?

Note the asymmetry in the definition: the *left* translates $x S$, $x \in X$, are required to
be pairwise disjoint, while the *right* translates $S x$, $x \in X$, are required to cover $G$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)

open MulOpposite
open scoped Pointwise

namespace Kourovka.«8.9»

/--
A group $G$ has *property $P$* (in the sense of C. Chou) if for every finite subset $F$ of $G$
there are a finite subset $S \supseteq F$ of $G$ and a subset $X \subseteq G$ such that the left
translates $x S$, $x \in X$, are pairwise disjoint, i.e. $x_1 S \cap x_2 S = \emptyset$ for all
$x_1, x_2 \in X$ with $x_1 \ne x_2$, and the right translates $S x$, $x \in X$, cover $G$, i.e.
$G = \bigcup_{x \in X} S x$.

Here the left translate $x S$ is `x • (S : Set G)` and the right translate $S x$ is
`op x • (S : Set G)`, following the Mathlib convention for right cosets.
-/
def HasPropertyP (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ F : Finset G, ∃ S : Finset G, F ⊆ S ∧ ∃ X : Set G,
    X.PairwiseDisjoint (fun x => x • (S : Set G)) ∧
    ⋃ x ∈ X, op x • (S : Set G) = Set.univ

/-- Every finite group has property $P$: take $S = G$ and $X = \{1\}$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem hasPropertyP_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : HasPropertyP G := by
  intro F
  cases nonempty_fintype G
  refine ⟨Finset.univ, Finset.subset_univ F, {1}, Set.pairwiseDisjoint_singleton _ _, ?_⟩
  simp

/--
(C. Chou). We say that a group $G$ has *property $P$* if for every finite subset $F$ of $G$,
there is a finite subset $S \supseteq F$ and a subset $X \subseteq G$ such that
$x_1 S \cap x_2 S$ is empty for any $x_1, x_2 \in X$, $x_1 \ne x_2$, and
$G = \bigcup_{x \in X} S x$. Does every group have property $P$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.9» : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], HasPropertyP G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.9»

items: `S \supset F` and `X \subset G` are read as non-strict inclusions (F ⊆ S, X ⊆ G), the Kourovka Notebook's standard usage. A strict reading of S ⊋ F would make the trivial group (F = G) fail property P and trivialise the question, so non-strict is clearly intended.

Finite subsets F and S are modelled as `Finset G`; the arbitrary subset X as `Set G` (no finiteness or nonemptiness imposed, as in the source). S is coerced to `Set G` so that no `DecidableEq` is required.

Left translate x S is `x • (S : Set G)` and right translate S x is `MulOpposite.op x • (S : Set G)`, following Mathlib's convention for left/right cosets. The asymmetry of the source (LEFT translates disjoint, RIGHT translates cover) is preserved exactly; membership characterisations were checked in a scratch file.
Disjointness `x₁S ∩ x₂S = ∅ for x₁ ≠ x₂ in X` is expressed as `X.PairwiseDisjoint (fun x => x • (S : Set G))`, which unfolds to exactly ∀ x₁ ∈ X, ∀ x₂ ∈ X, x₁ ≠ x₂ → Disjoint (x₁ • S) (x₂ • S).
Covering `G = ⋃_{x∈X} Sx` is expressed as `⋃ x ∈ X, op x • (S : Set G) = Set.univ`.
The universe of groups is quantified as `G : Type` (universe 0), matching the other Kourovka files (1_40, 19_25, 1_74).

An extra `@[category test]` lemma `hasPropertyP_of_finite` (every finite group has property P) is included to exercise the bespoke definition, as CONTRIBUTING.md asks for basic API tests of bespoke definitions.

reviewer_notes: Ambiguities: the notebook writes `S ⊃ F` and `X ⊂ G`; these are read as non-strict inclusions (standard Kourovka usage). A strict reading of S ⊋ F would make every finite group fail for F = G and trivialise the question, so non-strict is clearly intended; all candidates agreed. Boundary cases checked: X = ∅ gives an empty union ≠ univ (groups are nonempty), so no degenerate witness; X = {1} makes disjointness vacuous but forces S = G, only possible for finite G (this is the shipped test lemma). answer(True) = every group has property P, answer(False) = some group lacks it. No candidate omitted the slot; there were no omission reasons to weigh. Final file is byte-identical to c04.
